1_1.headline: Get management trained
missed: The training should cover the goals of § 38(3) BSIG: recognising and assessing risks and risk management, and judging what they mean for your company's services.
The law says only "regularly". Its explanatory memorandum reads that as training offered at least every three years (BT-Drs. 21/1501, p. 154). Neither sets how long a training lasts.

learn.title: Training for management
body: Whoever runs the company takes part in information security training regularly. This applies to every member of management personally.
We offer a course for this on this platform. You can also choose any other provider; the law does not require providers to be accredited.
learn.duty: Management has to take part in training regularly. The law sets no interval; its explanatory memorandum reads “regularly” as at least every three years.
learn.link: Go to the free course for management

record.title: What records can look like
record.caption: One line per person and training:

rows.name: Anna Example, managing director
rows.detail: In-person training at a training institute, 12 March 2026, certificate of attendance

rows.name: Jonas Sample, managing director
rows.detail: Online course, 3 April 2026, certificate as a PDF

rows.name: Lea Specimen, managing director
rows.detail: Webinar by an industry association, 20 May 2026, screenshot of attendance

record.note: The law prescribes no format. In-person training, an online course, a webinar or an in-house session all come into question. Record who took part, when, and what it covered.

trainings.title: One line per person
trainings.lead: Enter the latest training for every member of management. You can attach proof; after a webinar there is sometimes none.
